lxc_bc505ce37239647d.text:
In France, friends and family often say hello with la bise. La bise is a light kiss on the cheek. The cheek is the soft side of the face. Usually the lips do not really touch the face. People touch cheeks and make a small kiss sound. Then they do the same on the other cheek.

How many kisses? That depends on the place. Mathieu Avanzi studies languages. From 2016 to 2019, Mathieu Avanzi asked thousands of people about it online. In most of France, people give two kisses. In parts of the south, such as Languedoc, they give three. In east Brittany and around the Loire, many older people give four. In Finistère, at the far west of Brittany, many people give only one. People in France joke about it. You can guess the city by counting the kisses!

Nobody knows how la bise started. It is very old. In the south, men often kiss male friends and family too. In the north, two men who are not family usually shake hands.

In the USA, a kiss is not the normal hello. People shake hands when they meet someone new. A handshake is also the usual greeting at work. Close friends and family often hug. One reason is personal space. When they talk, people in the USA like about 1.2 metres of space. Many people in Europe stand closer, about 60 to 90 centimetres. A cheek kiss puts two faces very close. For most Americans, that is too close for a hello. Miami is different. There, a kiss on the cheek is much more common. In Japan, people bow. They move their head and body down and do not touch.

lxc_4da6eb8a07a62d5b.text:
In a restaurant in the USA, people pay for the food. Then they add a tip. A tip is extra money for the waiter. The Pew Research Center asked people in the USA about tips in 2023. Of people who sit and eat in restaurants, 81% said they always tip. For a normal meal, a little more than half give 15% or less. About a quarter give 20% or more.

Why is the tip so important? Because of the law. The minimum wage is the lowest pay a boss can give. Under national law, it is $7.25 an hour. Many states have a higher minimum wage. Workers who get tips are different. Under national law, the boss can pay them only $2.13 an hour. This number has not changed since 1991. With tips, the pay must get to at least the minimum wage. If it does not, the boss pays the difference. So tips are often most of a waiter's pay. In 43 states, tipped workers can get less from the boss. Seven states, such as California, give them the full state minimum wage.

Tipping came from Europe. In the 1850s and 1860s, rich Americans traveled to Europe. They copied the custom at home. They wanted to look like important old families in Europe. After the Civil War, the Pullman train company needed workers. In the late 1860s, it started to give jobs to Black men. Most of them had been slaves. They worked as porters. A porter carries bags and helps people on trains. Pullman paid the porters very little. So they needed tips from the passengers.

Many people in the USA hated tipping. Between 1909 and 1926, six states made tips against the law. But these laws did not work. In 1919, the USA decided to stop selling alcohol. Alcohol is in drinks like beer and wine. The law stopped people from making and selling these drinks. This was Prohibition. Restaurants could not sell wine or beer, so they lost money. So owners used tips to pay their workers. The custom stayed. In Japan, people do not usually tip.
